subject: Training-on-customer-data opt-out confirmation / Data handling follow-up
messages:
From: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@acmefin.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: data handling & training-on-customer-data

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned on the privacy items we discussed:  

- Scope: AcmeFin will evaluate Redwood for transaction categorization and downstream insights. You flagged two main concerns: PII handling (account numbers, ssn) and whether data sent to Redwood is used for model training.
- Our defaults: hosted API does not use customer data to update public models unless explicit opt-in is enabled; we do offer a training-on-customer-data opt-out that prevents customer inputs from being used for model improvement.
- Retention & logs: we keep request/response logs for debugging and billing by default; retention is configurable.
- Data residency: we can pin processing to us-east for this account.

Next steps:  
1) Can you confirm AcmeFin wants the training-on-customer-data opt-out applied across all routes?  
2) Please confirm retention window you require for request logs (30/90/365 days).  
3) I’ve attached the opt-out form and a DPA with suggested redlines for your legal team to review.

Attachments: RIN_training_opt_out_form.pdf, DPA_redlines_acmefin_v3.docx

I’ll loop in Dev for the technical confirmation once you confirm the opt-out and retention window.

Thanks,
Connor Obrien
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0147

From: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@acmefin.com>
To: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data handling & training-on-customer-data

Connor —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the following from AcmeFin:  

- We want the training-on-customer-data opt-out enabled for all API routes used by our team.
- For request/response logs: our security team prefers a 90-day retention window. We may request 30 days for production logs and 90 for audit logs — can you confirm if Redwood can support tiered retention?
- Data residency: yes, please pin processing to us-east.

Also: can you confirm whether embeddings computed for our text will be persisted or available to other customers? We need assurance that embeddings are treated as customer-owned and not used for cross-customer searches or model updates.

Sara Jensen
Head of Security & Privacy
AcmeFin
sara.jensen@acmefin.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@acmefin.com>, Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data handling & training-on-customer-data

Hi Sara —

Thanks for the confirmation. Short answers up front, followed by what we’ll do to implement the opt-out:  

- Training opt-out: we can enable a tenant-level flag that prevents any customer inputs (raw text, embeddings, deltas) from being included in aggregated model improvement pipelines. This flag is effective immediately once set.
- Embeddings: by default embeddings are stored for caching/perf but are not used for cross-customer searches or model training when opt-out is enabled. For extra assurance we can store embeddings encrypted with a customer-specific KMS key and set access controls so they remain only accessible to your account.
- Retention: Redwood supports configurable retention policies. We can implement tiered retention: 30 days for production request logs and 90 days for audit/billing logs. If AcmeFin prefers a single 90-day retention across the board that’s also feasible.
- Data residency: we will pin processing and storage to our us-east region for your tenant.

Planned implementation steps (timeline estimates):  
1) Legal finalizes DPA redlines (Connor to coordinate) — start: asap, target: 2 business days after receipt.
2) We enable tenant training-opt-out flag (Dev) — effective immediately once set; I’ll confirm by reply when done.
3) Configure retention windows (Dev) — target: within 24 hours of opt-out enablement.
4) Apply KMS-backed encryption for embeddings if requested (requires KMS customer onboarding; estimate 5-7 business days).

I’ll attach a short config example for our ops team. Let me know if you want the opt-out applied only to certain routes or all routes; we’ll default to all.

Attachments: training-opt-out-config.json (ops example)

From: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@acmefin.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data handling & training-on-customer-data

Sara —

Great — thanks for the quick confirmation. Per Dev’s note we will:  

- Apply training-on-customer-data opt-out at the tenant level across all routes.  
- Configure tiered retention: 30 days for production request logs, 90 days for audit logs.  
- Pin processing to us-east and ensure embeddings are KMS-encrypted (we’ll start KMS onboarding unless you tell us not to).

Next steps from AcmeFin:  
1) Legal: sign the attached DPA redlines or send back final comments. I’ve attached the DPA we sent previously (DPA_redlines_acmefin_v3.docx) — please let me know when legal is ready and I’ll generate a DocuSign envelope.  
2) Ops: confirm if you want KMS onboarding now or after pilot.

I’ll mark this thread as the official opt-out confirmation and update the tenant flag this morning. I’ll reply once the tenant-level opt-out and retention changes are live.

Thanks,
Connor Obrien
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com
